findings.message: Teaching case illustrations and hypothetical examples: Fictional classroom scenarios (Mirpurkhas, Hyderabad, Sukkur, Nawabshah, Karachi, Tando Allahyar) are original instructional examples designed for pedagogy and do not represent empirical case studies or official school inspection records.

Headless review tooling constraint: The crew job brief explicitly prohibits running npm run build, a dev server, or Playwright Chromium. Visual, structural, and presentation checks were conducted within permitted host resources via Sharp PNG rasterization with CSS variables resolved, SVG XML structure and token palette verification, and static heading/table container analysis.

Mapped reading availability: The course guide title Islami Nazriya-e-Hayat was not read or relied upon because author, edition and accessible text were not established in the spec. In accordance with D-2026-0001 and D-2026-0079, teaching is supported by the verified Qur'an translations, Bhat (2019), Sardar (2011), Met Museum and UNESCO resources, and the reading issue is tracked under existing intake issue G-2026-197.

Religious-content accuracy and specialized scholar review: In accordance with GISS-401 content-spec drafting note 2, substantive theological interpretations are standard and verified by this reviewer against Mustafa Khattab / Saheeh International paraphrases and Sahih Muslim hadith reports, but formal religious certification remains subject to the qualified Islamic Studies reviewer sign-off required for non-provisional publication.

UDHR text retrieval: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (Articles 1-3 and 17) cited in Topic 6.3 and declared under Unverifiable sources in sources/unit-06.md was independently verified during this G3 review session. The comparison between the Farewell Pilgrimage report (Sahih Muslim 1218a) and UDHR articles is strictly thematic, acknowledges distinct legal frameworks, and does not claim legal equivalence.
